excluded: Spinal nerve roots and cauda equina

limitations: Reference surfaces for education; not patient-specific anatomy or a clinically validated registration.
The HRA cord and BodyParts3D skeleton are different adult specimens. Axial scaling and centerline recentering explicitly adapt the cord to measured vertebral canal sections.
Cord segment names denote spinal cord segments, not the vertebrae at the same ordinal level. Segment positions after cross-atlas registration are approximate.
The cord follows one rigid torso frame during tracking; it does not bend with individual vertebrae.
Optic structures use one approximate global head registration and follow the tracked head, not eye rotation or gaze.
No peripheral limb nerves, nerve roots, cauda equina, separately named coccygeal cord segment, auditory/vestibular organs or retinal layers are present in this bundle.
Existing brain and eyeballs remain separate original head layers; the BodyParts3D spinal-cord alias resolves only a short canal surface and is deliberately not used as the full cord.

cord.anchorMethod: 81 horizontal sections over the middle 80% of each real vertebral source mesh; largest nested central lumen of area 0.5–12 cm² with center |x|<0.8 cm. Missing levels interpolate neighboring measured anchors.
cord.endpointConvention: Most superior HRA cord vertex maps to the measured C1 canal plane; most inferior maps to the measured L1 canal plane. This is an explicit cross-specimen reference fit, not patient calibration.
cord.method: Uniform axial/transverse scale; each original axial cross section recentered onto a piecewise-linear centerline through measured vertebral canal lumens. Original triangle topology retained; no tube or substitute cord generated.

head.method: Independent fixed BodyParts3D-to-MediaPipe canonical face similarity from head_frame.py; 80 iterations of 98% trimmed ICP; untrimmed frontal gate verified at build time.
